title: Typed positions are read as astropy reads them
claim: Degrees, letters, colons and spaces all give the position astropy gives, and nonsense is refused in plain words.
test: 28 strings, among them the challenge statement's own, were read by the page's parser and by astropy; 21 strings that are not positions must be refused.
pass_rule: Every position within 0.1 arcsec of astropy; every refusal has a plain message.

title: A star's catalogue position is moved to the date of a photo
claim: Proper motion, radial velocity and annual parallax move a catalogue position to the date of a photo as astropy moves it.
test: 10 stars (Barnard's Star, Epsilon Indi B, WISE 0855-0714 and seven fast Gaia DR3 stars) on 4 dates between July 2025 and September 2026.
pass_rule: Every position within 0.01 pixel (0.0615 arcsec) of astropy.

title: JavaScript and Python give the same visits, pairs and stacks
claim: The visit rule, the match rule, the background, the co-add, the resampling and the difference are the same rule in both languages.
test: Shared vectors written by Python are read by JavaScript; a vector written by JavaScript is read by Python. Real stamps of an empty field and of Barnard's Star are among them.
pass_rule: Visits and pairs equal; numbers equal within 1e-6 relative.

title: Alignment from field stars finds a known shift
claim: Cross-correlating the stars of two photos of one field finds how far one is from the other.
test: Five real stamps were shifted by four known amounts between 0.1 and 0.7 pixel with a cubic spline (scipy), and the shift was measured again.
